title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in Missouri's 5th Congressional District
description: Missouri's 5th Congressional District race has been dramatically reshaped by a Republican-drawn congressional map that was upheld by the Missouri Supreme Court in May 2026, extending the district from Kansas City eastward to rural Osage and Maries counties. The seat has been held since 2005 by Democrat Emanuel Cleaver, a former Kansas City mayor, who faces six Republican primary challengers and a Libertarian candidate. The new map makes the district more competitive for Republicans, though Cleaver has expressed confidence in his reelection bid and a citizens' referendum to overturn the map may appear on the November ballot. The Republican primary on August 4, 2026, will determine who challenges Cleaver in the general election.
polling_note: No recent public opinion polls were found for this race. The Cook Political Report has not yet rated the 2026 MO-05 race, and no independent polling firms have released surveys for this district. Polling may appear closer to the August primary or November general election.

candidates.name: Emanuel Cleaver II
candidates.summary: Emanuel Cleaver II has represented Missouri's 5th Congressional District since 2005 and previously served as mayor of Kansas City from 1991 to 1999. He is a Methodist minister and was a member of the Kansas City City Council. Cleaver has built a reputation as a moderate Democrat focused on housing, community development, and bipartisan cooperation. He faces a challenging reelection race after Missouri's new congressional map redrew the district to include more rural and conservative areas.

summary_sources.title: Missouri's new congressional map is moving forward. Who's running for Kansas City's 5th District?

candidates.name: Brad Patty
candidates.summary: Brad Patty is a retired U.S. Army Master Sergeant with 25 years of military service, running for Congress in Missouri's 5th District. He is from Fayette, Missouri, and holds an MBA. Patty's campaign focuses on cutting taxes, reducing federal spending, and fiscal discipline. He is one of six Republican primary candidates seeking to challenge incumbent Democrat Emanuel Cleaver.

summary_sources.title: Fayette resident files for US House

candidates.name: Brett Hueffmeier
candidates.summary: Brett Hueffmeier is an attorney and former aide to U.S. Senators Kit Bond and John Ashcroft, running for Congress in Missouri's 5th District. Born and raised in the district, he earned his law degree from Saint Louis University and has worked as a professor of business ethics and law. His campaign priorities include affordable housing, rural healthcare, and America First trade and economic policies.

candidates.name: Taylor Burks
candidates.summary: Taylor Burks is a U.S. Navy lieutenant commander and former Boone County Clerk who served as Boone County's first Republican county clerk. A fifth-generation Missourian and Navy veteran with three combat zone deployments, Burks has also served as director of the Missouri Division of Labor Standards and as president of Rost, Incorporated. His campaign emphasizes limited government, fiscal responsibility, and conservative values.

candidates.name: Rick Brattin
candidates.summary: Rick Brattin is a Missouri State Senator representing District 31 and a U.S. Marine Corps veteran, running for Congress in the state's 5th District. A former Cass County auditor and Missouri House member, Brattin is a self-described staunch conservative who has raised over $100,000 in individual donations. He entered the race in February 2026, positioning himself as a proven conservative leader.

summary_sources.title: Brattin Enters Race for Missouri's 5th Congressional District

candidates.name: Micah Beebe
candidates.summary: Micah Beebe is a Kansas City native and real estate professional running for Congress in Missouri's 5th District. He has over 13 years of experience in multifamily real estate transactions and describes himself as a conservative, Christian, pro-life candidate. Beebe is married with five children, including three adopted from the foster care system, and his campaign focuses on cutting taxes, securing the border, and supporting Missouri agriculture.
